title: Leeuwis2021: Left- vs right-hand motor-imagery EEG dataset
description: A single-session EEG dataset of left- versus right-hand motor imagery recorded from 55 healthy, BCI-naive participants using a 16-channel g.Nautilus system at 250 Hz. Each participant completed one calibration run without feedback and three feedback runs, for 160 trials in total. The data were collected to examine psychological and cognitive predictors of motor-imagery brain-computer interface performance. This BIDS release was converted from the original DataverseNL deposit via MOABB.
methods_description: Sixteen EEG channels (F3, Fz, F4, FC5, FC1, FC2, FC6, T7, C3, C4, Cz, T8, CP5, CP1, CP2, CP6) were recorded at 250 Hz with a g.Nautilus amplifier. The reference was the right earlobe and the ground was AFz. Participants imagined left- or right-hand movement following visual cues, with 5 s trials. The session had one calibration run without feedback and three feedback runs of 40 trials each, with 20 trials per class per run.
